newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RIVALS CLOSE GAP ON EUROPE'S PACESETTERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RIVALS CLOSE GAP ON EUROPE'S PACESETTERS.

text.p: The respective league leaders in Italy, Spain and England all endured disappointing weekends as their rivals took the opportunity to close the gap at the top.
Sampdoria's 4-1 home win over Cagliari and Internazionale's 2-1 success at Napoli cut Juventus's lead to two points in serie A following the world club champions' goalless draw with Atalanta.

Real Madrid and Liverpool also failed to find the net in goalless draws against modest opposition, and are now in danger of being overtaken by Barcelona and Manchester United who both have a match in hand.
Italy
The playmaking skills of Sampdoria's Roberto Mancini and Inter's Youri Djorkaeff breathed new life into the Italian title race on Sunday.

Veteran Mancini, tipped for a recall to Cesare Maldini's Italy side, made three goals in Sampdoria's impressive win at home to Cagliari while Frenchman Djorkaeff made one and scored another in Inter's 2-1 win at Napoli.
The results took full advantage of Juventus's 0-0 draw at home to Atalanta, leaving Sampdoria and Inter second on 28 points from 16 matches.
Juventus, who led by six points at the turn of the year, have managed only two points in their last three matches. Spain
Real Madrid threw away an opportunity to extend their lead in the Spanish first division when they were held to a goalless draw at bottom-placed Extremadura.

The outcome left Real three points ahead of Barcelona, who will take over at the top if they win Monday's game with Hercules. Third-placed Deportivo lost ground by drawing 1-1 at Valladolid but champions Atletico Madrid hit their best form to demolish Zaragoza 5-1.
Sevilla had new signing Robert Prosinecki to thank for the two goals which beat Oviedo, including a last-minute effort which clinched the match.
England
David Beckham added another spectacular goal to his collection as Manchester United beat Tottenham Hotspur 2-1 to move into second place in the English premier league.

London-born Beckham, who trained with Tottenham as a schoolboy, sealed Spurs' F.A. Cup exit at Old Trafford a week ago with a superb free kick and struck again 14 minutes from time from 25 metres to deny the home side a precious point.
Beckham, set to be a crucial member of the England side in this year's World Cup qualifying campaign, had previously had a quiet afternoon in one of United's less impressive performances.

The midfielder collected the ball jiust inside the Spurs' half and strode forward before crashing a right-foot shot into the top corner. United now have 41 points, two behind Liverpool who drew 0-0 with West Ham on Saturday. France
Nantes, unbeaten in their previous 17 matches, crashed out of the French League Cup when they lost to second division Louhans-Cuiseaux 4-2 on penalties after a 0-0 draw following extra time.
Louhans' upset second round victory left them the only non-first division side in the quarter-finals.
Brazilian striker Anderson scored a first half hat-trick as Monaco, who needed a penalty shootout to defeat second division Troyes in the first round, won 3-1 at second division Le Mans.
Third division giant-killers Nimes, who reached the French Cup final in May, lost 1-0 at home to Montpellier on Friday and are now out of both domestic cup competitions.
